svg.title: Vasicek vs CIR
svg.desc: Vasicek applies the OU process to rates; CIR scales the diffusion with the level and rules out negative rates.
svg.text: Vasicek vs CIR — Short Rate Models
OU applied to rates vs a diffusion term scaled by the level
Constant σ — independent of the level
AR(1) — simple by OLS or ML
If 2κθ ≥ σ² it never reaches zero
Euler schemes need truncation at zero
the functional forms of A and B differ
Moves by the same amount regardless of the level
The lower the level, the smaller the shock
Volatility is constant regardless of the rate
Same swings at low rates, so it goes negative
goes to zero as r does
It does not manufacture excess volatility at low rates
Both share the same mean-reverting drift; only the diffusion term differs.
Once the diffusion becomes σ√r, negative rates are ruled out and the law turns chi-square.
They share the same form of solution, but
but A and B take different functional forms
A continuation of Brownian Motion vs OU — Vasicek is the OU process with the state relabelled as a rate.
